# C++ audit 03: Multithreaded sum with a data race

**Date:** 2026-11-26
**Bug class:** data race
**Sanitizer that reproduces it:** ThreadSanitizer (`-fsanitize=thread`)
**Generated by:** an AI coding assistant, from the prompt below, for this repository
**Files:** [`buggy.cpp`](buggy.cpp) (generated code + test driver), [`fixed.cpp`](fixed.cpp)

## Task given to the model

```text
Speed up summing a large vector<int> in C++ by using 4 threads.
```

## Generated code (the part that matters)

```cpp
long long total = 0;
...
threads.emplace_back([&, begin, end] {
    for (std::size_t i = begin; i < end; ++i) {
        total += data[i];  // each thread adds its part to the total
    }
});
```

## Without a sanitizer: wrong, and differently wrong each time

The expected sum of 1 … 1,000,000 is 500000500000. Plain builds printed:

| Build | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clang++ -O0` | 277340855713 | 203533353796 | 233848868137 |
| `clang++ -O2` | 406250375000 | 250000250000 | 218750125000 |

At `-O2` whole threads' contributions seem to vanish: 250000250000 is exactly half the expected total. That fits the compiler keeping `total` in a register inside each thread and storing it once at the end. The compiler is allowed to do that, because a data race is undefined behavior and it may assume no other thread writes `total`. I inferred this from the numbers and didn't check the assembly. At `-O0` individual `+=` updates are lost. Neither result can be relied on.

## Reproduction

```sh
clang++ -std=c++17 -g -fsanitize=thread -pthread buggy.cpp -o buggy && ./buggy
# On recent kernels TSan may need: setarch -R ./buggy  (or sysctl vm.mmap_rnd_bits=28)
```

```text
WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race (pid=125)
  Read of size 8 at 0x7fffffffeaf8 by thread T2:
    #0 operator() 03-parallel-sum-data-race/buggy.cpp:18
  Previous write of size 8 at 0x7fffffffeaf8 by thread T1:
    #0 operator() 03-parallel-sum-data-race/buggy.cpp:18
```

Both accesses are line 18, `total += data[i]`, from two different threads, on the same 8-byte address: the stack variable `total`, which every lambda captured by reference (`[&]`).

## Root cause

`total += x` is a read, an add and a write. Four threads do it on one shared non-atomic `long long` with no synchronisation. The C++ memory model defines that as a data race, which is undefined behavior, not just "sometimes loses an update". The `[&]` capture hid the sharing: the lambda's comment says "each thread adds its part", but nothing gives each thread its own part.

| # | Severity | Location | Issue | How I confirmed it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | critical | line 18 | Unsynchronised `+=` on shared `total` from 4 threads (data race, UB) | TSan report; wrong totals in plain builds |
| 2 | major | line 16 | `[&]` captures everything by reference, which hides which state is shared | code reading |
| 3 | minor | line 11 | `thread_count == 0` divides by zero | code reading; guarded in `fixed.cpp` |

## Fix options considered

| Option | Correct? | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `std::mutex` around `total += data[i]` | yes | one lock per element: slower than a single thread |
| `std::atomic<long long> total` | yes | one contended atomic add per element: still slow |
| **Per-thread local sum, combine after `join()`** | yes | no shared writes in the loop: actually parallel |

`fixed.cpp` uses the third option. Each thread sums into a local variable and writes it once to `partial[t]`, its own element. After `join()` (which provides the happens-before ordering), the main thread adds the partial sums. It runs clean under TSan and returns 500000500000.

## Verdict

**Reject.** The result is wrong on every run, and the code is undefined behavior.

## What I would tell the model next time

"Name every variable that more than one thread touches and say how it's synchronised. Prefer per-thread results combined after join, and test under `-fsanitize=thread`."
